text: dsh-workbuddy 是面向 DSH 网页端的空白会话首页界面插件，为会话欢迎区换上 Wordless 风格。它注册并替换品牌标记与工作区菜单两个界面槽位，显示品牌图形、工作区列表和当前选择，并可通过目录选择流程添加工作区。菜单支持键盘导航、搜索式首字母跳转、加载和错误提示；原生工作区触发按钮与消息输入区仍由 DSH 管理。适合希望调整空白会话首页外观并继续使用现有工作区切换流程的用户。需要 DSH 网页客户端及相应界面、槽位、语言和工作区服务。

dsh-workbuddy restyles the DSH web blank-session hero with a Wordless-style brand mark and workspace menu. Users can select workspaces, navigate by keyboard, and add one through a directory picker. The host keeps its native trigger and composer. Requires DSH web UI and workspace services.
想把 DSH 空白会话首页的品牌标记和工作区菜单换个样式。
希望在网页端用键盘浏览并切换 DSH 工作区。
I want to restyle the blank-session workspace picker in the DSH web app.
dsh-workbuddy 的功能「首页品牌与工作区菜单换肤」：它替换空白会话欢迎区的品牌标记和工作区菜单槽位，列出工作区并标示当前选择；可用键盘移动、提交和按名称首字母跳转，也可经目录选择流程添加工作区。
dsh-workbuddy 的功能「目录选择后添加工作区」：在菜单提供的添加入口打开已注册的目录选择流程；选定路径后调用 DSH workspaces 服务创建工作区，并切换到新工作区，失败时显示可重试的错误对话框。

dsh-workbuddy README · dsh-workbuddy：Wordless-style skin for the blank-session hero of [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`). Restyles the two hero slots — the **brand tile** and the **workspace picker menu** — with the warm, minimal look of [Wordless](https://github.com/Austin-Patrician/Wordless). The native dsh web composer (the dialog box) and the native picker chip are **never touched**.

dsh-workbuddy README · What it changes：| Slot | Kind | What you get |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `conversation.hero.brand.mark` | `single` | Lime gradient tile with the WorkBuddy `W` |
| `conversation.hero.workspace` | `single` | Wordless-styled menu, anchored to the host's chip |
| ↳ `conversation.hero.workspace.directoryFlow` | `single` | Child hole this entry declares, so directory pickers still work |
| `conversation.composer.bar` | — | **Untouched** — the original dsh dialog stays |

dsh-workbuddy README · What it changes：Both target slots are `kind: 'single'`, so the plugin uses `ctx.slots.inject` to supersede the shipped occupants rather than adding alongside them. Each slot is injected independently — `inject` waits for its slot to be declared, so chaining would couple the workspace occupant to the brand-mark slot's lifetime.

dsh-workbuddy README · How the picker slot works：`conversation.hero.workspace` is **not** a welcome panel. The host (`ConversationRoot`) renders the trigger chip itself and owns the open state; the slot occupant is only the menu body, and it receives:

dsh-workbuddy README · How the picker slot works：| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `open` | Whether the picker is expanded — the occupant renders `null` while closed |
| `anchorRef` | Ref onto the host's trigger chip, used to position the menu |
| `selectedId` | Currently active workspace (rendered with a trailing check) |
| `onPick` | Choose a workspace; the host connects or reuses its blank session |
| `onClose` | Dismiss — bound to <kbd>Esc</kbd> and to any press outside |

dsh-workbuddy README · How the picker slot works：The menu is `position: fixed` and measured from the anchor rect, so it escapes the hero's `overflow: hidden auto` scroll body; it flips above the chip when there is no room below.

dsh-workbuddy README · How the picker slot works：| Key | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd> | Move the cursor, wrapping at both ends |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | Jump to the first / last row |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Commit the row under the cursor |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Close, and hand focus back to the host's chip |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> / <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> | Close and hand focus back, rather than leaving an open menu sitting behind whatever was tabbed into |
| Any printable character | Typeahead — jump to the next row whose name starts with it; press it again to cycle through rows sharing that initial |
dsh-workbuddy README · How the picker slot works：Three details the keyboard route depends on, each of which a simpler implementation gets wrong:

dsh-workbuddy README · How the picker slot works：- **Focus enters on the cursor's row, not on the menu container.** A cursor that starts at row 0 has to already own focus, or the first <kbd>↓</kbd> steps to row 1 and the top of the list is silently skipped.
- **The cursor opens on the host-reported selection**, so the operator sees where they are before moving — and is clamped on read, so a refresh that removes rows from under it still leaves one row carrying `tabindex=0`. Unclamped, the menu would keep rendering while quietly ceasing to be keyboard-navigable.
- **A pending snapshot reads as loading, not as empty.** Before the workspace list arrives, "no workspaces yet" is a flash of a wrong answer.

dsh-workbuddy README · Adding a workspace still works：The host's `renderSlot` call carries **no** creation callback, so a reskin that renders only the list would silently drop the hero's "Add workspace…" action. This entry avoids that the same way the shipped picker does — by supplying the missing half itself:

dsh-workbuddy README · Adding a workspace still works：Adopting a picked directory is one interaction at a time: while the flow is open or a path is being adopted, every row is disabled. A rejected `createWorkspace` surfaces in a retryable dialog rather than vanishing, and an occupant that unloads mid-interaction withdraws the flow so the rows come back.

dsh-workbuddy README · Adding a workspace still works：That dialog is a real modal: it traps <kbd>Tab</kbd> inside itself (as `aria-modal` promises rather than merely declares), closes on <kbd>Esc</kbd>, and hands focus back to the host's chip when dismissed — except on retry, where the picking flow takes focus instead and the two do not fight over the same keystroke.

dsh-workbuddy README · Adding a workspace still works：> The hero exposes no slot for a welcome headline or entry chips — `hero.headline` is hardcoded copy in the host, not a slot. A Wordless-style welcome panel therefore has nowhere to live without fighting the host layout; this plugin reskins what dsh actually offers.

dsh-workbuddy README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin add ml020/dsh-workbuddy
```

dsh-workbuddy README · Design：Tokens live in `src/client/styles/tokens.module.css`, scoped under `.root` with a `--wb-*` prefix so they never collide with dsh's own `--dsw-*` theme variables. Light and dark follow `prefers-color-scheme`.

| Token | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workspace | `#fbfbfa` | `#151610` |
| Sidebar | `#f1f1ee` | `#202219` |
| Accent | `#ccf257` | `#bfe650` |
| Selected row bg | `#eef4dc` | `#303a1c` |

Type is **Manrope** for UI and **DM Mono** for workspace paths.

dsh-workbuddy README · Layout：```
src/
  index.ts              host loader (no-op, browser-only plugin)
  invariant.ts          package-owned invariant companion
  client/

dsh-workbuddy README · Development：```bash
npm install
npm run typecheck     # tsc --noEmit (no errors)
npm run test          # vitest run
npm run lint          # oxlint

The dsh UI client packages are `__ModuleLoader__` bundles that only run inside the dsh web host, so the browser specs exercise the plugin against the doubles in `tests/mock-slots.ts` instead of importing them.

dsh-workbuddy README · Screenshots：`docs/*.png` are photographed from the real components rather than drawn. `preview/` mounts `BrandMark` and `WorkspaceMenu` inside a host-accurate dsh shell with Vite, and Playwright shoots it at 2× in light, dark and selected states.

```bash
cd preview
npm install
npx playwright install chromium   # once per machine
npm run shoot

dsh-workbuddy README · Screenshots：One detail the harness handles: the menu focuses its cursor row when it opens, and with no prior input the browser credits that scripted focus as a *keyboard* focus and paints `:focus-visible` into the shot. The harness blurs before capturing, so the previews show what clicking the chip actually looks like.

dsh-workbuddy README · Screenshots：`npm run check:bundle` exists because nothing in `tsc`, `vitest` or `oxlint` looks at `lib/`, and the failure mode is silent. The host loads the client half as a CommonJS closure factory with a specific banner and footer, and resolves every cross-plugin import through its own module table: drop the footer, or let the bundler inline React, and the package still builds, still passes every test, and throws at load time in a browser console nobody is watching. The checks are asserted against the artifact after a real build, and CI runs them the same way.
